question: Which of the following is true regarding the bud development process in Hydra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell divisions at one site**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bud development in Hydra is initiated by a series of cell divisions at a specific site on the body column.
 
• These cell divisions result in a localized growth, forming a bud that eventually develops into a new individual.
 
• The budding process allows Hydra to reproduce asexually, producing genetically identical offspring.
 
• Buds remain attached to the parent organism until they mature, at which point they detach and become independent Hydras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydra**

 
 
• A genus of small, freshwater organisms that belong to the phylum Cnidaria.
 
• Known for their regenerative abilities, allowing them to repair or regrow damaged parts.
 
• They have a simple body structure with a tubular shape and a mouth surrounded by tentacles.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**
 
 
• A mode of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes.
 
• Produces offspring that are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
• Common methods include budding, binary fission, and fragmentation.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**
 
 
• The process by which organisms replace or restore lost or damaged tissues.
 
• Hydra can regenerate an entire organism from a small fragment of its body.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Cnidaria**
 
 
• A diverse group of aquatic animals that include jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones.
 
• Characterized by the presence of cnidocytes, specialized cells used for capturing prey.
